Consult Summary:
32-year-old postpartum female with sudden onset dyspnea one hour ago; clinician concerned for possible pulmonary embolism and advised immediate hospital evaluation.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute shortness of breath, postpartum (1 hr onset)
- Sudden dyspnea while seated watching TV; first episode.
- Associated: non-productive cough since yesterday; mild chest soreness on deep inspiration; subjective palpitations (“heart really going”).
- No frank chest pain; no hemoptysis reported.
- Post-cesarean section 4 weeks ago (hypercoagulable risk).
- Family history: mother with leg clots.
- Examination (virtual): patient counted 30 heart beats during timed interval (clinician noted “slightly fast” HR); no other vitals available.
- Clinical impression: rule out pulmonary embolism vs other cardiopulmonary causes.

Issue 2: Post-operative status post elective C-section (4 weeks)
- Ongoing incisional tenderness.
- Analgesia with Codeine; last dose approximately 1 week ago.
- No other postoperative complications mentioned.

Issue 3: Medication allergy
- Ibuprofen allergy; reaction not specified.

Medications:
- Codeine – dose/route/frequency not documented (last taken ~1 week ago).

Allergies:
- Ibuprofen (reaction not documented).

Past Medical History:
- Cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
- No other chronic conditions mentioned.

Social History:
- Lives at home with newborn; partner at work at time of call.
- Smoking, alcohol, occupational history not discussed.

Preventative History:
- Not addressed during consult.

Physical Examination:
- Heart rate: patient self-counted 30 beats during unspecified interval; clinician interpreted as tachycardia.
- Chest: tenderness on deep inspiration; C-section scar tender.
- No other vitals or exam findings documented.

Plan:
- Advise immediate presentation to nearest hospital emergency department for assessment of possible pulmonary embolism (consider D-dimer, imaging, anticoagulation if confirmed).
- Offered ambulance; patient opted to self-transport promptly with infant.
- Avoid further Codeine until evaluated.
- Take essentials for baby to hospital.
- Reassured patient; advised to seek help sooner if symptoms worsen en route.
- No routine follow-up arranged; hospital team to assume care.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: full vital signs (BP, RR, SpO₂, temperature), complete medication and allergy details, obstetric history specifics, smoking/alcohol status.
● Internal conflict: Patient stated DOB 20 Apr 1980; clinician restated 1983 (conflict noted). 
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; some conversational redundancies removed.
